learningObjective: Explain FlashAttention's core algorithmic idea: block-tiled attention with online softmax and backward recomputation of the attention matrix.

canonicalClaims.claim: FlashAttention is an exact attention algorithm that block-tiles Q, K, V and uses online softmax to avoid materializing the N x N attention matrix in HBM; the backward recomputes the attention probabilities from stored (m, l) row statistics rather than reading them from HBM.
conditions: SMEM is large enough to hold the tile of Q, K, V, and softmax stats.
Sequence length N is such that the N x N matrix would otherwise be HBM-resident.
nonImplications: Does not change the O(N^2 d) FLOP count of attention.
Does not require lower precision (FP8) to be beneficial.

misconceptions.claim: FlashAttention is an approximation that trades accuracy for speed.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FlashAttention is bit-exact (up to rounding order) to standard attention; the win is I/O, not approximation.
It reduces HBM I/O, not FLOPs; FLOPs remain O(N^2 d) (slightly more if backward recomputation is counted).

misconceptions.claim: FlashAttention gains come from FP8 or reduced precision.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FA v1/v2 use FP16/BF16 like standard attention; the speedup comes from HBM traffic reduction.
It is a dense, exact algorithm; pruning is a separate line of work (sparse attention).

implementationFacts: Forward stores per-row (m_i, l_i) statistics of size O(N); backward needs these plus Q, K, V to recompute P.
Backward performs an extra O(N^2 d) pass to reconstruct P block by block.
performanceScenarios: Speedup grows with sequence length N because the avoided HBM traffic is O(N^2).
